title: _human_review_ledger.json -- DAO-only record of genuine human review decisions v0.1
description: One per case (leading-underscore shared state, like _conflict_ledger.json). Records every human decision that a machine-written contract is forbidden to self-declare: accepting a policy-audit finding as a residual risk, verifying an unpaged administrative exclusion, resolving a page/table to a human reading. Written ONLY through dao.py record-human-review, never through write-contract. Each record binds an immutable review UID to the exact bytes of the artifact reviewed (artifact_sha256, computed by the DAO from the on-disk file at record time -- an agent cannot supply its own hash). A downstream contract that claims a human decision must reference a review_uid here; the DAO re-verifies the UID exists, the referenced artifact's current hash still matches artifact_sha256, and the recorded decision is one this artifact kind allows. This is the same trust model as mark-human-review-complete (the CLI invocation is trusted to be a genuine human action); what it removes is the ability to fabricate 'a human decided X' inside a machine-authored JSON contract with a bare name string.

case_id.description: Widened from exactly 3 digits to 3-or-4 on 2026-08-22. This was the ONLY schema pinning an exact width -- every other case_id in the repo is `^CASE_[0-9]+$` -- and that single outlier set a hard 999 ceiling on the whole id space, because `fork_case.next_free_case_id` must not mint an id this ledger would later refuse. With CASE_9001/9200/9401 already on disk the ceiling was permanently exceeded, so every fork silently fell back to reusing the lowest free gap (CASE_054 on 2026-08-22), losing chronological order. Existing 3-digit ids stay valid; nothing needs renaming.

review_uid.description: Immutable content-derived identifier, computed by the DAO from case_id|artifact_kind|artifact_id|target_key|artifact_sha256|reviewed_at. Never supplied by a caller.

reviewer.description: The human reviewer's identity, as recorded by the trusted CLI invocation (same accountability field as mark-human-review-complete --reviewer and set-ledger-status).

artifact_kind.description: Which class of decision this is. Determines which downstream contract may reference the record and which decisions are allowed. classification_review covers a document_type classification produced from PRE-REDACTION page text (classification_text_source: raw_page_text), which is permitted but must not finalize unreviewed -- see classification_result.schema.json.

artifact_id.description: The document the reviewed artifact belongs to (e.g. the audit's / parent-coverage's source document).

target_key.description: Identifies the specific item within the artifact the human reviewed: a finding_uid for policy_audit_finding, or a 'physical:<N>' physical-page key for unpaged_physical_exclusion. For classification_review it is the fixed string 'classification_text_source:raw_page_text' -- the condition that raised the flag.

artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact on-disk artifact bytes at record time, computed by the DAO. A downstream reference is only honoured while the current artifact still hashes to this value -- editing the artifact after review invalidates the human decision, which must then be re-made.

decision.description: The human's disposition. accepted_risk: a policy-audit finding is a known, accepted residual risk. verified: an unpaged exclusion is a genuine administrative page. rejected: the reviewed item is wrong and must not be relied on downstream (never satisfies a completion gate). For classification_review, 'verified' means a human read the classification produced from pre-redaction text and confirmed the label stands -- in practice by checking that the evidence quote survives redaction, since a label reachable from the redacted layer had no PII doing load-bearing work.

note.description: The human's rationale. Required -- a decision with no stated reason is not a review.
